title: Asymmetric Perturbation in Solving Bilinear Saddle-Point Optimization

split.decision: User decision 2026-10-29: original Leduc for validation; one independently secret-seeded terminal-payoff perturbation for hidden evaluation (zero-sum, unchanged tree, multiplicative factors uniform [0.95,1.05]). No training instances. Both instances independently solved at prediction time. Hidden construction metadata only in operator records. Protocol v2 preserves the original game files privately and interprets a bounded declarative graph IR. Only trusted oracle traversals execute on the game; combined update counts are authoritative.

baseline.paper_ref: Figure 4 Leduc; reproduced rounded NashConv 0.0013945 after 1000000 combined updates; paper has no tabulated scalar.
baseline.timing_scope: legacy protocol estimates retained for operational budgeting; not a measured v2 reference

judge.scientific_memory_note: Original configured 8 GB retained. Execution adds an 8 GiB per-process address-space safeguard (or lower operator cap); aggregate physical-memory equivalence is not certified.

conversion.reason: Task-side numeric API compatibility corrections. Original game, metric and update budget retained.

leakage_remediation.verification_scope: Two original asymmetric runs x 2 sweeps, three nondefault numeric graph families, shared graph/process counts, one-core isolated train/predict/scorer, fresh clone. No full reference.

experiment_preservation.numeric_api_compatibility: verified for recorded default and nondefault cases; not exhaustive arbitrary native graph programs

allowed_changes: Game solvers, auxiliary regularizers, numeric graph structure, permitted stochastic updates, optimizers, regularizer schedules and hyperparameters other than the step size may change within the verified graph interface.
The baseline asymmetric DGDA formulas and mu are methods, not mandatory target games; eta stays fixed at 0.1; generic adaptation to counted updates and declared-policy snapshots is permitted.
fixed_contract: Improve last-iterate equilibrium approximation for the fixed Leduc zero-sum game and the fixed hidden payoff-perturbed instance, using the counted solver interface.
The original information-set/action tree, legal strategy simplexes, actual zero-sum payoffs and frozen hidden instance remain fixed; computational regularization does not redefine these game targets.
The original NashConv, final current policies combined as player1 from run0 and player2 from run1, and aggregate limit of 1000000 sweeps / 2000000 counted single-player traversals remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
